record.original_question: Let S be a semigroup and let X be any set. A semigroup conjugacy relation on S is partition-covering if, for every partition of X, one can put a semigroup structure on X whose conjugacy classes are exactly the blocks of that partition. For the standard semigroup conjugacy relations ∼o, defined by a ∼o b when there exist g,h in S with ag = gb and bh = ha; ∼p, defined by a ∼p b when there exist u,v in S with a = uv and b = vu; and ∼tr, the epigroup relation defined using idempotent powers a^ω and b^ω together with elements g,h satisfying ghg = g, hgh = h, hg = a^ω, gh = b^ω, and ga^(ω+1)h = b^(ω+1), must every partition arise as the set of conjugacy classes of some semigroup?

evidence.quote: To investigate whether some analogous structure exists for semigroups, Problem 6.10 from [3] asks whether the conjugacies studied therein are partition-covering.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an arbitrary nonempty set. For a semigroup $S$, define the following equivalence relations on $S$ (called semigroup conjugacy relations):

(1) $a \sim_o b$ iff there exist $g,h \in S^1$ with $ag = gb$ and $bh = ha$.

(2) $a \sim_p b$ iff there exist $u,v \in S^1$ with $a = uv$ and $b = vu$.

(3) (Defined on epigroups, where each element $a$ has a power $a^n$ lying in a subgroup of $S$, with idempotent $a^\omega$ denoting the identity of that subgroup, and $a^{\omega+1} = a \cdot a^\omega$.) $a \sim_{tr} b$ iff there exist $g, h \in S$ such that $ghg = g$, $hgh = h$, $hg = a^\omega$, $gh = b^\omega$, and $g\, a^{\omega+1}\, h = b^{\omega+1}$.

A semigroup conjugacy relation $\sim$ is called partition-covering if for every partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ there exists a semigroup structure on $X$ whose $\sim$-classes are exactly the blocks of $\mathcal{P}$.

Question: Are each of $\sim_o$, $\sim_p$, and $\sim_{tr}$ partition-covering?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is answered affirmatively: each of the standard semigroup conjugacy relations $\sim_o$, $\sim_p$, and $\sim_{tr}$ (along with $\sim_c$, $\sim_n$, $\sim_{p^*}$) is shown to be partition-covering, resolving the cited Problem 6.10.

status_evidence.title: Partition-covering conjugacies of semigroups (arXiv:2411.16284)
status_evidence.claim: All the listed standard semigroup conjugacy relations are partition-covering, answering the question affirmatively.
